_readme: Hand-written copy for each project, in Ahmed's own voice: confident and direct, crediting teams and clients. Overrides role / tagline / summary / highlights from the synced project.json files, so re-running `npm run sync` never undoes it. Leave a field out to fall back to the synced text.

yalla-kora.tagline: A World Cup 2026 app for football fans, sold through mobile operators
yalla-kora.summary: A phone-first football app that mobile operators sell to their subscribers: live scores, fixtures, match centres, predictions and a daily quiz. Fans arrive from a text message on a mobile connection, so I built it to load fast and read naturally in Arabic and Kurdish, under four operator brands.
highlights: Match centres organised into focused tabs: events, stats, line-ups and head-to-head
A timed daily quiz designed to be quick and fair on a phone
Arabic and Kurdish (Sorani) right-to-left layouts, light and dark themes, and a skin for each operator
A Next.js server layer that keeps subscriber sessions private and off the client

snap-games.tagline: Swipe, play, level up: a game feed for mobile subscribers
snap-games.summary: A game app sold through mobile operators in Iraq and Nigeria. Players swipe through a feed of HTML5 games, play in one tap, and earn points toward nine levels. I built the feed, the game player and the progression screens in Arabic, English and Kurdish.
highlights: A vertical feed that launches each game in a sandboxed frame, with full screen and a rotate prompt
Nine levels and daily streaks that bring players back
The right language and reading direction from the very first paint

3abee.tagline: One voucher store, four operator brands, four currencies
3abee.summary: A store where subscribers buy gift cards, game credit and subscriptions and pay through their phone bill. I built it as one Next.js app that ships as four branded stores, for Sudani, Syriatel, Chinguitel and STORE 70 in Senegal, each with its own look, languages and currency.
highlights: Four brands from one codebase, selected at build time
Arabic, English and French, with Sudanese, Syrian, Mauritanian and West African currencies
Direct game top-up by player ID, alongside voucher cards
A test suite that keeps every brand working as the others change

lumio.tagline: A kids' streaming app: shows, short clips and characters to collect
lumio.summary: A streaming app for Arabic-speaking children aged three to eight, with a PIN-protected area for parents. I built it in React Native from the team's design system, right-to-left from day one, with progress that survives a weak connection.
highlights: Shows organised by season, plus a short-clip feed made for small hands
Daily watching unlocks characters children collect
Playback progress saved on the device and synced later, so nothing is lost offline
Every colour and size comes from design tokens, enforced in the build

lumio-website.tagline: The public website for the Lumio kids’ app
lumio-website.summary: The site parents land on before they install Lumio: the shows, the characters, how the app keeps children safe, and the pages the app stores require. I built it in Next.js, right-to-left, with one config file driving the store links, legal pages and social previews.
highlights: One download link that sends iPhones to the App Store and Android phones to Google Play, used on QR codes, SMS and ads
A QR code on desktop so parents can move straight to their phone
An account-deletion form with validation, spam protection, rate limiting and a request ID that can be read out over the phone
Store badges that switch to “coming soon” on their own when a listing isn’t live yet

first-step.tagline: The staff portal that runs a football, padel and tennis academy
first-step.summary: First Step Academy's staff run their day from this portal: booking fields, checking availability, and tracking payments and expenses, all in Arabic. I designed the booking flow to be fast enough to use while a customer waits at the desk.
highlights: A step-by-step booking flow with live availability per field in half-hour slots
A shared tennis timeline that shows at a glance how busy each slot is
Owner reports: income, peak hours, unpaid bookings and expenses
Runs on Cloudflare Workers with a D1 database, so it costs the academy very little to host

first-step-customer.tagline: Players find a free field and request a booking in three steps
first-step-customer.summary: The public side of First Step Academy. Players choose a sport, a date and a time, see what's free, and send a booking request that lands straight in the staff portal. They can look up their bookings with just a name and phone number.
highlights: Three steps from picking a time to confirming on WhatsApp
Availability across football, padel and tennis in one grid
Requests go directly into the staff portal's inbox

first-step-mobile.tagline: The academy's staff app for booking and checking the day on the go
first-step-mobile.summary: A React Native companion to the First Step portal for staff who are out on the fields, not at the desk. It covers today's schedule, booking, the bookings list and monthly finances, all in Arabic.
highlights: The portal's booking flow, rebuilt for one-handed use
Today's and this month's income at a glance
Connects to the live portal, or runs on sample data for training

tennis-booking.tagline: A tennis club booking portal built around one shared court timeline
tennis-booking.summary: I adapted the First Step portal for a club with four tennis courts. Staff see how many courts are taken in every half hour in a single view, then assign the player a free court.
highlights: One timeline for all four courts instead of four calendars
Shows which courts and durations are still open for the chosen time
Its own deployment and database, independent of the academy

kinetiq.tagline: One offline-first app for Pilates studios, CrossFit boxes, dojos and gyms
kinetiq.summary: A product I designed for gyms of every kind, with dedicated screens for owners, coaches, the front desk and members. It keeps working when the gym's internet doesn't, and each gym only sees the features it needs.
highlights: Separate experiences for owners, coaches, front desk, a TV display and members
Built-in tools for each kind of gym: reformer spots, workout leaderboards, belt progress
All data stored in the browser and synced later, so check-ins never stop
Feature flags that turn modules on per gym, plan or vertical

ims.tagline: Lab inventory that tracks every lot and expiry date
ims.summary: An inventory system for hospital laboratories, where staff need to know what's on the shelf, what expires soon and what to order next. It recommends which lot to use first, explains its reorder suggestions, and works fully in English and Arabic.
highlights: Recommends the lot that expires first, and records a reason for any override
Reorder levels calculated from the lab's real usage, with the working shown on screen
Approval chains for sensitive actions such as disposing of stock
A handheld layout for storekeepers with barcode scanning

roost.tagline: The phone app that runs a home daycare: two-tap logs, automatic parent reports
roost.summary: Home daycare providers have their hands full, so logging a nap or a meal takes two taps, and parents get a daily report automatically. It works without internet and syncs when a connection returns.
highlights: Two-tap logging for meals, naps, nappies, incidents and medication
An automatic daily report page for parents
Attendance, drills and documents compiled into an inspection-ready record
An offline-first sync engine designed so no entry is ever lost

hax-oi.role: Built the site with the HAX team
hax-oi.tagline: A pilot platform matching experienced executives with the right opportunities
hax-oi.summary: The website for an executive advisory service in the Gulf. Visitors learn about the service and complete a short review of their experience, which the team uses to prepare tailored opportunity notes. I built it to handle personal data carefully and to stay within the client's approved wording.
highlights: A multi-step review that tells each applicant clearly whether the service fits
Opportunity notes that separate facts, interpretation and unknowns
Privacy-first analytics that strip personal details before anything leaves the browser

shopraha-dashboard.tagline: The back-office for an online grocery in Kuwait
shopraha-dashboard.summary: The admin tool ShopRaha's operations, content and customer care staff used every day, built on the open-source Saleor dashboard. I built the grocery-specific modules: recipes, delivery slots, deals and customer wallets.
highlights: A recipes section where every ingredient links to a product customers can add to their basket
Delivery time slots and return pickups for the operations team
Buy-one-get-one, bundle and wallet cashback deals for the marketing team
Grocery details such as price per kilo and units of measure

cockpit.tagline: The operations dashboard for orders, catalogue, marketing and deliveries
cockpit.summary: ShopRaha's internal operations dashboard, connected to both the shop's GraphQL API and the delivery service. I built the catalogue, marketing campaigns, customers and the main dashboard, while teammates built the delivery tools.
highlights: A route planner where dispatchers drag deliveries into routes on a map
Delivery zones drawn on the map, with capacity per time slot
Banners, cashback, vouchers and featured products in English and Arabic

btr-smooth.tagline: The portal online shops use to manage orders, stock and deliveries
btr-smooth.summary: Smooth lets online shops in Kuwait store products in BTR's warehouse and have them delivered. Merchants use this portal to follow orders, send in stock, run reports and top up their account. It's part of a shared monorepo of internal tools.
highlights: A single timeline per order, from warehouse shelf to the customer's door
Downloadable reports for merchants' own records
API hooks generated from the backend schema, so the frontend never drifts from it

btr-rover.tagline: A dispatch dashboard for route planning and driver schedules
btr-rover.summary: The tool dispatchers use to plan delivery routes, manage drivers and vehicles, and set how many deliveries each hour can take. I contributed frontend features alongside the team that built it.
highlights: Route planning from unassigned orders on a map
A weekly shift grid for drivers
An hourly view of delivery load against capacity

btr-halo.role: Built by my BTR teammates, on shared packages I worked on
btr-halo.tagline: Warehouse management: receiving, stock and picking
btr-halo.summary: The warehouse system for ShopRaha's fulfilment centres: receiving stock, putting it away and picking orders. My teammates built this app on the shared monorepo packages I contributed to.
highlights: Receiving with barcode, quantity and expiry for every line
A visual editor for laying out aisles and racks
Multiple warehouses and multiple merchants in one system

shopraha-app.role: Built by my ShopRaha teammates, on the backend and dashboards I worked on
shopraha-app.tagline: ShopRaha's grocery app for iPhone, Android and web
shopraha-app.summary: The customer app for ShopRaha, an online grocery in Kuwait. My teammates built the app; it ran on the backend, dashboards and services I worked on with them.
highlights: Browse aisles, search in Arabic or English and fill a basket
Choose a delivery slot and pay by KNET, card or cash
Track the order to the door

shopraha-web.tagline: ShopRaha's web shop and app-launch page
shopraha-web.summary: The ShopRaha web store from 2021–22 and the landing page for the app launch, built by the team. It's included to show the full product the dashboards served.
highlights: Aisle pages, product pages and a slide-in basket
Checkout with saved addresses and delivery slots
Arabic by default, with English

aod.tagline: An Android experiment: a ring of light around the camera while the phone sleeps
aod.summary: An Android app that draws a soft ring of light around the front camera while the screen is off, with twelve light patterns and colours for notifications. The demo is a web simulator running a direct port of the app's drawing code.
highlights: Twelve light patterns, from a slow breath to a charging ring
Each app's notifications tint the ring in its own colour
A calibration screen, because phones don't always report where the camera really is
Battery-friendly rendering with a capped frame rate and subtle drift to protect the screen

aiwin.tagline: Website and product catalogue for a Jordanian waterproofing manufacturer
aiwin.summary: I moved AIWIN, a Jordanian maker of bitumen waterproofing and insulation, from an old WordPress site to a fast static site. Engineers and contractors can find every product and download its technical data sheet.
highlights: A page for every product, with photos and a downloadable data sheet
All content in one structured source, easy for the client to update
Fully static: fast to load and nearly free to host

soho-cafe.tagline: A live QR menu for a hotel restaurant, café and lounge in Amman
soho-cafe.summary: A digital menu for SOHO Midtown Hotel in Amman. Guests scan a QR code at the table and see the current menu, pulled straight from the hotel's point-of-sale system, so staff never update it twice.
highlights: Separate menus for the restaurant, lobby, room service and minibar
Search in English and Arabic
Reads directly from the hotel's POS, hiding staff-only items

heartfeltcode.tagline: The site for my consultancy for non-technical founders
heartfeltcode.summary: The website for Heartfelt Code, my consultancy helping early-stage founders without a technical co-founder turn an idea into a working product. A fast static site with almost no JavaScript, case studies and a contact form.
highlights: Fast and lightweight, with almost no JavaScript
Case studies written as problem, what we built, and the outcome
Light and dark themes with accessible contrast

drift-academy.tagline: A landing page for a drift driving school
drift-academy.summary: A one-page site for Raafat Haroun's drift academy, written in Jordanian Arabic, presenting the courses, the coach and a booking form.

augment-clone.tagline: A layout study rebuilding an existing landing page in Next.js
augment-clone.summary: A study where I rebuilt the layout of augment.org's landing page in Next.js and Tailwind to learn from its design. The original design and most of the text belong to augment.org.

eliteshop.tagline: A storefront with catalogue filters, cart and checkout
eliteshop.summary: A storefront I built to work with animation and client-side state: a home page with deals, a filterable catalogue, a wishlist and a cart drawer. The demo adds sample products and a simulated checkout.
highlights: Catalogue search with category, price and sort filters
Cart and wishlist that persist across reloads
Light and dark themes

gym-pwa.tagline: A gym member app that installs on the phone
gym-pwa.summary: A progressive web app for gym members: check membership, browse exercises and log sets, then install it on the phone like a native app.
highlights: A workout logger for sets, reps and weights
Installs on the phone and opens offline

saas-starter.tagline: A starting point for SaaS apps: sign-in, teams, roles and billing
saas-starter.summary: A foundation for software-as-a-service apps with sign-in, organisations, roles and billing models. The demo adds sample pages so the layout can be explored.
highlights: Organisations with owner, admin and member roles
A dashboard layout that works on phones and desktops

sports-booking.tagline: A prototype for booking football pitches and padel courts
sports-booking.summary: A React Native prototype for booking a football pitch, a padel court or a hall at a sports centre, in Arabic and English.
highlights: A four-step booking flow: place, date, time and payment
Arabic and English with a live language switch
